gaps: Method note: I downloaded all 10 Artificial Analysis model pages (claude-haiku-5-5[-low|-medium|-high|-xhigh] and claude-sonnet-5-5[-low|-medium|-high|-xhigh]) on 2026-10-16. Intelligence Index score, cost per task, total output tokens, output speed and TTFT are quoted from the pages' visible summary or FAQ sentences. Every other metric (output tokens per task, GDPval-AA Elo and its cost per task, AA-Briefcase Elo, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience hallucination rate, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode) is shown on these pages only as rendered charts. Those values come from the Next.js chart data embedded in the same page HTML, identified by model slug and field name. They are AA's unrounded stored values, written as fractions where AA stores fractions; I did not round them or convert them to percentages.

Index version: every page states 'Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 incorporates 10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1'. That is the same version the existing Opus/Fable texts cite. No per-page 'last updated' date is shown. The release dates (Haiku 5.5 2026-10-07, Sonnet 5.5 2026-09-28) come from the page data and the visible 'Released October/September 2026'.

Cross-check against existing texts: the Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 max rows embedded on the Sonnet 5.5 page match what the texts already cite: Opus 57.62 / $5.98 per task / GDPval 1866.27 at $8.918 per task; Fable 53.35 / $7.63. This confirms all four models sit on one v4.3.2 scale. I did not re-fetch the Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.1 low/medium/high/xhigh pages, so only their max rows are recorded here.

Discrepancy, not recorded as a claim: search-result snippets attributed to news coverage (officechai.com, oodaloop.com) said Sonnet 5.5 at max costs '$7.60 per task' and uses '~193,000 output tokens per task'. I did not open those articles, and the AA page currently shows $5.46 per task and 197430.37 output tokens per task. Treat the press figures as unverified or out of date.

Discrepancy within the AA pages: the visible total-output-token sentences (Haiku max 440M, Sonnet xhigh 110M, Sonnet max 420M) do not match the embedded canonicalIntelligenceIndexTokenCount.output values (435183286, 105144665, 415769956). The page does not explain the difference; the visible figure may count something extra, such as repeats. Both are recorded in the quote field.
Ultracode (many-agent workflow) effort level: Artificial Analysis does not report it for any model; the AA effort variants are low, medium, high, xhigh and max only.

Haiku 5.5 long-prompt pricing ($0.50/$2.50 beyond 100K-token prompts): not shown on the AA pages. They list only $0.10 input / $0.50 output, a 90% cache discount and a $0.01 cache-hit price. The AA cost per task is computed at the base price.

Naming: Sonnet 5.5 variants are labelled '(<Level>, Default Fallback)' on AA. Haiku 5.5 variants are currently labelled '(Low)' through '(Max)' with no 'Default Fallback' suffix, although search-index titles for the Haiku pages showed 'Default Fallback'. A non-reasoning variant is mentioned only generically ('A non-reasoning variant may also exist'); no page for one was found.

Not looked at: the AA leaderboard (artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models) and the Intelligence Index methodology page. The per-model pages already carried the per-level data, so those pages could only add rank context. Separate GDPval-AA, AA-Briefcase and Omniscience leaderboard pages were also not checked.
Not opened: the Anthropic launch posts and system cards for Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. They were outside this Artificial Analysis evidence family, so there are no third_party=false claims.

Local working files (outside the repository): the downloaded HTML, parsed text and extracted JSON are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-glow-hdengine-v2/30dbddec-e6c8-51a7-8b5f-7b64d3484280/scratchpad/aa, and the parsing scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-glow-hdengine-v2/30dbddec-e6c8-51a7-8b5f-7b64d3484280/scratchpad/tools. Nothing was written to the repository, Notion, GitHub or any other external service.
